Grand Theft Auto 6 delayed again, but it'll still ship in 2026
Mark your calendars for November 19, 2026
- Rockstar Games has confirmed another delay for GTA 6
- Grand Theft Auto 6 will now release on November 19, 2026
- It's all in the quest to deliver an 'unrivalled experience'
The wait for the next Grand Theft Auto is now even longer as Rockstar Games – and its parent company, Take-Two Interactive – have announced yet another delay, pushing the release date for GTA 6 to November 19, 2026.
After sharing the new date, which is six months after the previous release date of May 26, 2026, in a released statement, Rockstar Games writes, “We are sorry for adding additional time to what we realize has been a long wait, but these extra months will allow us to finish the game with the level of polish you have come to expect and deserve.”
Any Grand Theft Auto title is a massive game, and GTA 6 looks to leapfrog even that of GTA 5.
And it does make sense that Rockstar Games wants to ensure it gets the next chapter in the universe right, correct?
GTA 6 is set to return to us a modern Vice City, dubbed Leonida, and follow the story of two protagonists, Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval.
It’s a much-anticipated title, and Rockstar Games does hit on that with the conclusion of its statement:
“We want to thank you again for your patience and support.
While the wait is a little longer, we are incredibly excited for players to experience the sprawling state of Leonida and a return to modern-day Vice City.” The move from Spring – May 26, 2026 – to Fall/Winter – November 19, 2026 – brings the launch closer to the holiday season as well.
Rockstar Games also confirmed the new release date on X (formerly Twitter), and during Take-Two Interactive’s earnings call, CEO Strass Zelnick wrote in a statement, “We remain both excited and confident they will deliver an unrivalled blockbuster entertainment experience,” after confirming the new timing.
Many were expecting an update on GTA 6 during the earnings call, given we got other details and a full trailer in prior ones, but this is certainly not the happiest news for fans eager to play the title.
Rockstar Games seems more certain about this release date, and Zelnick's comments suggest it will ensure that when GTA 6 does release, it will be polished to the quality we expect, both in gameplay and story.

Binance pauses withdrawals after suspected $3B+ hack as Tether, Circle freeze $2.4B
Summary
- Binance paused withdrawals on several networks after more than $3B was drained from its hot wallets in a suspected hack.
Tether and Circle froze $2.4B in stablecoins, but over $1B, mostly ether, is beyond reach.
Binance says user funds are safe.
The market has largely moved past the initial shock.
BNB has bounced off its low and bitcoin is steady near $78,800, which suggests traders see the freezes and CZ’s pledge as limiting the damage to Binance itself.
The next risk is supply.
The attacker holds more than $1 billion in ether and has already been selling smaller tokens on decentralised exchanges, so large ETH sales could weigh on ether’s price.
Partial withdrawal pauses at the world’s biggest exchange also tighten liquidity before Friday’s monthly options expiry on Deribit at 08:00 GMT.
---
Earlier:
- Binance appears hacked, CZ says, as Tether and Circle freeze $1.79B in stablecoins
- Tether freezes $971M USDT amid suspected Binance hack as crypto sells off
---
Binance has stopped part of its withdrawals and stablecoin issuers have locked up $2.4 billion, but the ether that got away keeps this suspected hack on course to be crypto’s largest.
Summary:
- Binance temporarily paused withdrawals on multiple networks after more than $3 billion was drained from its Ethereum hot wallets on 29 October.
- Tether froze more than 1.567 billion USDT and Circle more than 800 million USDC, about $2.4 billion in total.
More than $1 billion, mostly ether, remains unfrozen.
- Binance says user funds are completely safe but hasn’t called it a hack or given a loss figure.
CZ says it looks like a hack and expects losses to be covered.
- The attacker used EIP-7702, an Ethereum feature that lets a wallet run contract code, from an address funded through Tornado Cash.
- BNB fell to about $692 before recovering to around $704.
Bitcoin is near $78,800.
- If confirmed, the theft would more than double Bybit’s record $1.5 billion hack in 2025.
Binance has paused withdrawals on several networks after more than $3 billion was drained from its Ethereum hot wallets late on Thursday, 29 October, in what co-founder Changpeng Zhao says looks like a hack.
Tether and Circle have together frozen about $2.4 billion in stablecoins, but more than $1 billion, mostly ether, remains out of reach.
Binance spokesperson Ross O’Leary told TechCrunch the exchange had temporarily suspended withdrawals on multiple networks as a precaution.
Binance has said user funds are completely safe and that withdrawals will resume once the security issue is fully resolved.
It has not used the word hack, given a loss figure or explained how the funds left.
An early version of its statement on X said it had not confirmed any impact on user funds, and it was later edited to say funds were safe, FinanceFeeds reported.
Zhao, who stepped down as chief executive in 2023 but remains Binance’s largest shareholder, said user funds are safe and that he expects them to be fully covered.
Tech-ish reported that he later put the loss after freezes at about $1 billion, possibly a little higher, and said Binance would cover it.
The freezes are larger than first reported.
Tether chief executive Paolo Ardoino said more than 1.567 billion USDT had been frozen, up from the roughly $971 million Zhao cited earlier.
Circle said it froze more than 800 million USDC in coordination with law enforcement.
About 700 million USDT left the receiving address before Tether’s blacklist took effect, and much of it was swapped into ether, according to Tech-ish.
On-chain data points to an outside attacker.
A wallet labelled Binance 14 was linked to a smart contract set up by an address funded through Tornado Cash, a crypto mixing service.
The attacker used EIP-7702, an Ethereum feature that lets an ordinary wallet run contract code.
Minutes later, a single transaction moved about 167,000 ETH, roughly 1.6 billion USDT and 62 other tokens to a new address.
The attacker has since been selling tokens the stablecoin issuers cannot freeze, including UNI and PEPE, on decentralised exchanges.
Some tallies circulating on X put total outflows above $5 billion, but those include bitcoin and Tron movements not yet tied to the attacker.
Crypto markets steadied after the initial drop.
BNB, Binance’s own token used for trading-fee discounts and fees on its affiliated BNB Chain, fell from about $739 to a low near $692 before recovering to about $704 by 22:15 GMT, CryptoTicker data showed.
Bitcoin was near $78,800 and ether around $2,265.
About $628 million in leveraged positions were liquidated within an hour, mostly longs.
If confirmed, the Ethereum transfers alone would more than double the $1.5 billion stolen from Bybit in February 2025, the largest crypto theft on record, which the FBI attributed to North Korea.
Traders will watch for a formal Binance loss figure and reimbursement plan, whether the attacker dumps its ether on the market, and how quickly withdrawals reopen.
